name: Steel, re-rolling mills and metal fabrication

problems.words: Weight at our kanta and the customer's kanta never match
quick_ideas: Photograph the weighbridge reading for every truck — gives both sides the same evidence
Agree in advance with regular parties which kanta counts — ends the argument at the gate.

workzap_build.text: a weighbridge log where each truck's weights, reading photo, gate pass and invoice are tied together automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do you have your own weighbridge or use an outside kanta?
problems.free_stops: How readings are captured and matched is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note your kanta weight and the customer's kanta weight for each truck this week, so the mismatch pattern by route or party stands out.
Give one dispatch person the job of writing both weights on each delivery note, so disputes stop bouncing between yard and sales.

problems.words: Burning loss is higher than it should be but I can't prove where it goes
quick_ideas: Record scrap charged and output per heat for one week — shows which heats or shifts lose most
Compare shifts side by side — points to where to look.

workzap_build.text: a heat and shift yield register showing burning loss per heat daily with trends.

problems.ask_first: Is burning loss recorded per heat or per day now?
problems.free_stops: The yield calculation and alert levels are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare scrap charged and finished output for each heat in one week, so the heats with unusual burning loss stand out clearly.
Give one furnace record keeper one page for every heat's charge and output, so loss tracking stops breaking across loose slips.

problems.words: Booked customers at the old rate, now steel has gone up
quick_ideas: List every open booking with tons and rate — shows your real exposure
Set a time limit on how long a booked rate holds — limits future risk.

workzap_build.text: a rate-booking ledger of booked tons, booked rate, delivered tons and open exposure, updated with each dispatch.

problems.ask_first: How often do you book at a fixed rate in advance?
problems.free_stops: Booking rules and exposure limits are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each old-rate booking with the latest mill purchase rate in one notebook, so you spot which promised jobs now squeeze cash.
Keep one open-booking page beside dispatch papers and give one clerk the daily update, so expired price promises stop slipping into production.

problems.words: Dealers delay payment and keep rolling over balances
quick_ideas: Rank dealers by oldest balance once — tells you who to chase first
Fix a limit per dealer — gives the sales desk a clear line.

workzap_build.text: a dealer ledger with limits, ageing and automatic reminders, visible to whoever books orders.

problems.ask_first: What's the oldest balance you're chasing?
problems.free_stops: Limit rules and reminder timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which dealers took fresh tonnage while their oldest invoice stayed unpaid this week, so you see whose dispatches are stretching your cash cycle.
Give one dispatch-side person one shared dues list to check at booking time, so sales promises and outstanding balances stop drifting apart.

problems.words: Customers call for the day's rate and nobody has the same number
quick_ideas: Decide one person who sets the day's rate — removes conflicting numbers
Send that one rate to all sales staff each morning — everyone quotes the same.

workzap_build.text: a daily rate broadcast of one approved rate to all dealers on WhatsApp, with booking confirmations recorded.

problems.ask_first: How do you share the day's rate today?
problems.free_stops: The approval and broadcast set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the rate each caller receives from different sales staff on the same day, so you can see where the quote mismatch starts.
Give one person the job of writing the day's rate in one shared place each morning, so every branch quotes the same number.

problems.words: Scrap yard stock is a guess and material walks out at night
quick_ideas: Do one physical count of the yard by type — gives a true starting figure
Allow no truck out without a gate pass matched to an invoice — closes the obvious leak.

workzap_build.text: a yard stock board with cycle counts and a digital gate pass that must match an invoice before a truck leaves.

problems.ask_first: How often is the yard physically counted now?
problems.free_stops: Count routine and gate rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the scrap yard once and note rough piles by type and outgoing trucks by night, so unusual stock movement has a visible baseline.
Give one gate person one notebook for every outgoing load after dark, so missing material is tied to a single nightly record.

problems.words: Fabrication jobs always finish late and I can't see why
quick_ideas: List open jobs by stage (cutting, welding, painting, installation) once — shows where they stall
Get photo proof from site at handover — settles "done or not done".

workzap_build.text: a fabrication tracker by stage with site photos, showing late jobs daily.

problems.ask_first: Where do jobs usually get delayed?
problems.free_stops: Stage set-up and site sign-off flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each open fabrication job under its current stage on one wall sheet, so the queue causing late finishes becomes visible.
Give one floor supervisor the job of updating job stage at the same time daily, so handovers stop losing where work is stuck.

problems.words: We quote fabrication jobs by experience and lose on half of them
quick_ideas: Compare actual steel, consumables and labour hours with the quote on recent jobs — shows where estimates go wrong
Charge separately for drawing changes after cutting — stops rework eating margin.

workzap_build.text: a job costing template comparing steel weight, consumables, labour and overheads with the quote on every job.

problems.ask_first: Do you work to client drawings or your own?
problems.free_stops: Costing method and change-order terms are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare quoted steel, labour time and rework notes against finished jobs this week, so the part of the estimate that misses most stands out.
Give one estimator one notebook for quote assumptions and later actuals on each job, so repeat underquoting stops hiding inside experience.

problems.words: Welders are paid per piece and disputes happen every week
quick_ideas: Have the supervisor note pieces per worker role at the end of each shift — gives a shared record
Show the tally to the team before payday — disputes surface early.

workzap_build.text: a piece-rate output log visible to supervisor and staff, totalled automatically for payday.

problems.ask_first: Who records output on the floor now?
problems.free_stops: The output-log set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count finished pieces by worker role at shift end for one week, so the dispute size and timing become clear before payday.
Give one supervisor one tally page kept beside production for every shift, so piece counts are settled from one shared record.

problems.words: I don't know my cost per ton until the accountant closes
quick_ideas: Pick the four figures that drive cost per ton (scrap, power, labour, yield) — focuses the daily view
Ask for those figures weekly instead of monthly — catches problems sooner.

workzap_build.text: a morning read of tons produced, yield, power hours lost, cost-per-ton estimate and receivables.

problems.free_stops: How the estimate is calculated is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write yesterday's scrap used, power run, output and labour shift count in one notebook each evening, so cost drift shows before month end.
Make one shift clerk update the same cost notebook at a fixed closing time daily, so the accountant gets clean figures without chasing.

never_say: No structural design, weld procedure, load, metallurgy or grade-compliance advice.
Burns, falls, crushing, furnace or electrocution accidents: stop and point to emergency services first.
Never help tamper with weighbridge readings, under-invoice or adjust weights; decline.
Never help process scrap of unknown or suspected stolen origin.
No customs, import duty or tax advice; talk to your accountant.
Workers and contractors: roles and counts only, never names, CNICs or individual wages.

sample_reply.person: Koi solution do yaar. Har truck pe weight ka jhagra hota hai, hamara kanta kuch kehta hai party ka kuch aur.
sample_reply.pi: Ji, is ka hal mumkin hai aur shuruaat isi hafte ho sakti hai. 1) Har truck ki weighbridge reading ki photo lein, taake dono taraf ek hi saboot ho. 2) Regular parties ke saath pehle se tay kar lein ke kis kante ka wazan maana jayega. Workzap yeh aap ke liye khud-ba-khud kar sakta hai: weighbridge log jahan har truck ka wazan, photo, gate pass aur invoice apne aap jud jayein. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
